title: Hickman, Milneburg jobs and Burbank at Maison Blanche
summary: Playing with Hickman at Milneburg and with Burbank on advertising trucks for Maison Blanche.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What about this fellow Hickman?
Oh, he used to play saxophone, he used to play with Rene.
Alto Oteno was? Alto. What was his first name, do you know? Maybe that was his first name, I don't know. I forgot. His first name, yeah. Did he ever play with you much?

Not that much. We played quite a bit at the White Place, which he was leading up to play off the normal and advertised for Maison Blancenic. He had that job in charge. But he sticked with Rene for a long time.
Who was in the Meilenburg job with Hickman? Who else?
Louie Gallo, myself, on trumpet, and I think it was Albert George who played a drummer. That was what was Forrest was.
What did Gallo play then?
Piano.
They had pianos out there on the lake, huh? Oh yeah. I don't see how they ever moved them out there on those flanks.
They were out there.
They had them out there. Gosh, yeah.
Not on the pavilion, I mean this was on land.
Oh I see, out near the. Yeah, it was right out there, but on land. What was the name of the place? Got me there.
Been too long ago.
Did you ever work with Burbank?

Burbank worked with me. Yeah? Where? He played a lot of jobs with me off and on, and we played together for Maison Blanche, Annex. Well it was, he got the job, but most of the time he couldn't play, well I used to take the band over.
For Maison Blanche, Annex?

Yeah, they used to advertise once or twice every week. Instead of the papers what they had in the TV, we'd get on the street. We'd take uptown route in the morning, twelve o'clock we'd take a break for an hour, then we'd wake downtown in the afternoon.
That was on a truck?
About five years.
